headline: Math is nearly solved; agents and real work remain the frontier
outlook: Math has effectively saturated: math benchmarks closed 95% of their remaining headroom over the past year, and FrontierMath, FrontierMath Tier 4, ProofBench and ARC-AGI-2 all passed 90% between June and September. Agents and real work moved slowest, closing only 34% of headroom, and the spread within that category is wide: APEX-Agents jumped to 82.4% in recent weeks, while the Remote Labor Index sits at 21.2% and OSWorld 2 at 31.4%. Task length may connect the two. The longest tasks AI can handle have reached 17.4 hours and have been doubling roughly every 4.1 months, which on current trends points to work-week-length tasks around December, though the likely range stretches to August 2027. Cost is falling even faster: GPQA-level reasoning at 80% or above has dropped from $3.44 to $0.055 per million tokens, so the coming year likely brings very capable reasoning at very low cost, while a 90% Remote Labor Index score is not expected until early 2028. Hold all of these dates loosely, since past likely ranges caught the real date only 59% of the time, and the HLE and SimpleQA forecasts have each moved by more than seven months in the last three months alone.
